surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism for ALD of WS2 and SnS involves the sequential injection of precursors (WCl5 and H2S for WS2, tin(II) acetylacetonate and H2S for SnS) into the growth area, followed by purge cycles to remove excess species and by-products. The growth process enables precise control of film composition and thickness through layer-by-layer deposition.
evidence: ALD is a monolayer stepwise growth process where the reactants are alternately injected into the growth area, and following each reaction, excess species and by-products are purged out. The precursors for WS2 growth were WCl5 and H2S (9%, balance Ar). The WCl5 source temperature was set at 110 oC and the carrier gas (nitrogen) flow rate was 250 sccm. The pulse sequence per cycle was as follows; WCl5 pulse width was 0.8 s, N2 purge of 1.0 s, H2S pulse of 1.2 s, followed by 1.0 s N2 purge. The SnS films were grown from tin (II) acetylacetonate and H2S.
